title: Nexus
description: Nexus is a FastAPI + Celery + PostgreSQL/pgvector pipeline that turns a noisy social-media stream into a curated, continuously evolving map of "Event Hubs," so downstream applications can display curated, self-contained story views instead of raw feeds.
context: Social feeds are high-volume and fragmented: important posts are scattered across unrelated people, threads, and moments. Nexus brings related posts about the same real-world subject, event, or story into a continuously updated whole, giving people a clearer view of the bigger picture, helping them connect perspectives, understand what is happening, and discern meaning from fragmented information.
overview:
Nexus is a real-time event clustering platform: it turns a firehose of social posts into a continuously updated map of the stories happening in it. Each incoming post is embedded, matched against existing story hubs, and either assigned, parked as an ambiguous candidate, or rejected as noise. New stories emerge on their own through community detection over buffered posts, duplicate content is folded, and every decision is delivered to downstream applications through a transactional event log.
It is also a system that is meant to be correctable. Every automatic decision is journaled with the numbers that produced it. An operator can confirm or unlink any assignment, and those human corrections are the only signal the system learns from. A daily autotuner replays that history and proposes threshold revisions; a monthly job fine-tunes a LoRA adapter on the same corrections and promotes it only if it beats the current model on a held-out set.
What makes the project interesting is not the component list. It is that every meaningful decision came from measuring the actual system rather than trusting a reasonable default. The thresholds were recalibrated because the originals sat above the embedder's ceiling and produced silent failure. The parallelization was deleted because concurrency made throughput 10x worse. The noise filter was rewritten from a keyword list into a structural test after adversarial examples leaked through it. And the learning loop was restructured after an audit showed it was training on a positive it had curated itself, which meant it could never teach the model what the correct hub was.
Stack: PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector (HNSW), Celery with Redis, FastAPI, spaCy for entity extraction, a MiniLM transformer with a LoRA adapter, and a server-rendered operator panel. Everything runs on CPU.
problem:
The signal is sparse and distributed. The posts that matter to a single story are scattered across different people, different threads, and different hours. No individual reader assembles the full picture, so nobody can answer the only question that matters: what is actually going on here?
The obvious approach fails on identity. A similarity search over embeddings treats an Apple product launch and a Samsung product launch as near-identical text. Cluster a "phone launch" thread on embeddings alone and it fuses into one confident, wrong hub. The embedder has no concept of who is speaking, and cosine similarity cannot recover it.
Naive filtering throws away the important stuff. The usual approach to noise is a stopword list or a length threshold, but real feeds are full of text that looks substantive and isn't, and the important posts are often the ones that name nothing. "The two-year yield had its biggest one-day drop" is a genuine market event with no entity in it at all, and a noun-phrase filter discards it.
Automatic clustering cannot self-correct. A threshold that is slightly too loose accumulates errors invisibly. Worse, a system that learns from its own confident assignments learns to agree with itself, and its reported precision becomes fiction.
So the problem reduces to two questions that are much harder than they sound: recover identity from text, and decide what deserves to exist  reliably enough to trust either with automatic action.
solution:
Measure the embedder before trusting it. The original thresholds were conventional (0.80–0.95 cosine) and produced zero hubs and 0% coverage: not misclustering, complete silence, because the constants sat above the model's actual ceiling. Profiling real content showed same-topic similarities peak around 0.71 (mean ~0.50) while cross-topic text sits near 0.1. Every threshold was recalibrated against that measured scale. The same discipline killed other defaults  windowed embeddings stay at a 256-token head because tiling measured worse on live content, and near-duplicate folding sits at 0.98 cosine because folding is destructive and must be near-certain.
Resolve identity by evidence overlap, not string equality. The naive rule "posts sharing an entity belong together" breaks on a single cross-mention post, where "Apple's reveal is compared to Samsung's event" welds two disjoint stories together. Instead, two entity strings are the same actor only when their post sets overlap substantially (≥ 0.6 of the smaller set): aliases overlap near 1.0, rivals only on comparison posts at ≤ 0.56. What counts as identity is deliberately asymmetric  generic collective nouns ("insiders", "observers") are stripped because they appeared across every topic and would make all hubs look related; places are excluded because a hurricane legitimately spans several states; and people are included for vetoes but excluded from merge evidence, because "Musk" spans distinct Tesla and SpaceX threads.
Filter on structure rather than keywords. The gate rejects cheap cases (empty, too short, chatter, first-person diary) before spending anything on parsing, then admits anything carrying any independent route to substance: entities, proper nouns, debate structure, modality, a topical event lexicon, a claim hashtag, or a question. "Diversity drives innovation, period." clears on the verb drives with zero entities. Universal quantifiers are explicitly not evidence, because they appear constantly in filler.
Learn from operators, never from itself. Only explicit human corrections become training signal; system bookkeeping is stored and displayed but never graded. The learner was rewritten after an audit showed it had been training on a positive it curated itself, which meant it could not teach what the correct hub was. Positives now come from confirmed pairs, removed posts become hard negatives, and a post rejected after a merge moved it there counts as an even stronger negative. Promotion is gated on a holdout scored with the same metric, with the split hashing each post to exactly one side so nothing leaks. The autotuner proposes rather than applies, and scans the entire precision curve because precision is non-monotone a first-fit scan silently picks a worse point.
architecture:
Ingest. A durable row insert plus a bounded Redis hint queue. Redis is a latency fast path, never the source of truth, so an outage degrades to slower processing rather than lost posts. The row carries a content fingerprint computed at ingest, normalized conservatively so only byte-identical bodies collapse exactly; near-copies fall through to an embedding pass.
Process. Work flows through Celery to a single-flight CPU embedder, then the discourse gate, so chatter never costs an embedding. A worker claims posts with a compare-and-swap status transition, so concurrent workers can never process the same post twice.
Assign. A bulk chunk-level SQL pass: HNSW top-2 against fresh centroids in one statement, with a margin check between best and runner-up. An ambiguous post is parked as a candidate rather than guessed at. The HNSW index is partial, scoped to active non-null centroids, keeping the freshness window inside the index.
Discover. Hourly, buffered posts are partitioned into temporal slices, joined into a k-NN graph with exponential time decay (12h half-life), and clustered with Louvain community detection, guarded by multi-author and cohesion requirements. Because community detection over-splits (measured up to 34 hubs for 10 topics), a merge reconciliation to fixpoint runs immediately after birth.
Deliver. A transactional outbox with lease-based claiming via FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, a dead-letter queue, and TTL garbage collection, so a downstream outage becomes a recoverable backlog instead of a stalled pipeline. Every event carries a per-post monotone sequence, letting consumers drop stale deliveries and order events per post despite at-least-once delivery.
Merge and correct. All merge initiators funnel through one guarded transaction, so the outcome is identical regardless of who asked. Concurrent merges of the same pair serialize on an advisory lock taken on the ordered hub id pair, making deadlock structurally impossible. Merges snapshot their member set so reopening is exact rather than heuristic, and reopening recomputes centroids for both hubs from live members instead of restoring the frozen snapshot. Every mutation is versioned, journaled, and reversible.
Operate. Versioned advisory-locked migrations, structured JSON logging, a 49-route operator panel for curation, calibration, merges, and observability, and a fail-closed production posture where an unset auth token refuses to boot rather than serving open.
decisions: Similarity calibration :The conventional 0.80 to 0.95 defaults sat above the model's real ceiling and produced 0 hubs, 0% coverage. 1. Recalibrated every threshold against measured embedder distributions

Embedding: Running the embedder across a thread pool collapsed throughput from 10.7 to ~1.1 posts/s, cache thrash on one shared CPU model. Tiling the token window measured worse than the head window on live content. 1. Serialized the embedder under a single-flight lock 2. Kept a 256-token head window instead of tiling (0.24 to 0.47 tail vs 0.50 to 0.54 head)...

Identity evidence: Embeddings read identically across actors, so identity has to come from extracted entities. String matching alone welds unrelated stories together, and some entity types carry no identity signal at all. 1. Required ≥0.6 post-set overlap before treating two entity strings as one actor (aliases overlap ~1.0, rivals only on comparison posts at ≤0.56) 2. Excluded people from merge evidence but kept them for vetoes ("Musk" alone spans the distinct Tesla and SpaceX threads)

Pure keyword filtering throws away legitimate posts that name nothing, while loose heuristics admit filler as substance. 1. Built admission on structure (entities, debate markers, event lexicon) rather than stopwords ("the two-year yield had its biggest one-day drop" carries no entity at all) 2. Excluded universal quantifiers as evidence, since they appear constantly in filler and leaked adversarial noise

Learning loop:  A system that grades its own confident output learns to agree with itself, which makes reported precision fiction. 1. Never graded autocreated assignments as training signal 2. Rewrote the learner to take positives from human confirmations, because the original self-curated its own positive and so could never teach what the correct hub was 3. Treated rejections arriving after a merge as stronger negatives, since those posts travelled with the merge and were still refused

Concurrency and durability: Merges race against each other and against assignment, and fsync is not equally necessary on every write. 1. Partial HNSW index scoped to active hubs, so the 48h freshness window lives in the index rather than in a filter 2. Advisory lock over the ordered hub id pair for merges, since a consistent order makes deadlock structurally impossible 3. Snapshot merge membership so reopening is exact, restoring precisely what was merged and leaving later arrivals untouched

Event delivery Delivery is at-least-once and genuinely reorders, and holding row locks across network calls stalls the pipeline. 1. Per-post monotone sequence in every event, giving consumers an ordering and staleness key 2. Webhook I/O outside database transactions, releasing locks before network calls so rows left leased are reclaimed by lease expiry
features: Single and batch ingestion (up to 500 posts), consumer-token authenticated
Semantic assignment of posts to existing hubs with margin-based ambiguity handling
Automatic discovery of new hubs via temporal k-NN graphs and Louvain community detection
Entity-aware conflict resolution, so Apple and Samsung launches never fuse.  Repost folding: identical and near-duplicate content collapses to one member
Discourse gate that classifies chatter and diary posts as noise before embedding.  Transactional outbox with lease-based delivery, dead-letter queue, and TTL cleanup
Webhook push with HMAC signing and a circuit breaker. Reversible hub merges with canonical redirects
Per-post and per-hub subject views: catalyst post, timeline, perspectives, media, voices
Human-in-the-loop confirm/unlink on any assignment.   Decision journal: every automatic decision with similarity, margin, and versions
Feedback rollups with precision, coverage, unlink rate, and drift index.   Daily threshold autotuner with impact estimates and knob warnings.   Monthly LoRA fine-tuning with a promotion gate

Versioned, reversible policy and model history.   49-route operator panel: quality desk, merge desk, calibration, audit, ops, hub graph.   Admin accounts with PBKDF2 passwords, TOTP, Google sign-in, and session revocation
Fail-closed production posture, CSRF origin checks, security headers, per-consumer rate limits.
Structured JSON logging, health probes, and DLQ/stuck-post visibility
